purpose.question: Does the Gallery machinery remain coherent when evidence comes from different objects, different failure trajectories, and different standing states?
purpose.population_001_question: Can one cleanly bound source event be represented correctly through the frozen Gallery machinery?

what_population_002_tests.description: Binding to at least two distinct source objects, each with its own immutable commit coordinate, Git blobs, and SHA-256 identities
Manifestations from different trajectories, testing whether multiple lens memberships across entries from different objects remain non-contradictory
At least one entry whose source event has an unresolved, withheld, pending, or incomplete standing trajectory

recursive_eligibility_boundary.observation: Population 001 construction produced a preserved procedural failure (commit b9ad3c5, __dummy__ branch write, unreferenced commits, additive correction)
recursive_eligibility_boundary.constraint: A failure in the Gallery's own construction must pass through the same predeclared selection rule, source binding, entry cardinality, temporal standing binding, and non-promotion boundary as any other source event

ordered_gates: Admit this predeclaration; selection rule and procedure frozen before any event is evaluated against the Population 002 selection procedure

Enumerate and select events under the frozen selection procedure; enumerate, record, evaluate, and select by predeclared ordering rule; preserve qualifying but unselected candidates with ordering reason
Construct gallery entries with immutable source binding, lens memberships, boundary attribution, and temporal standing binding
Preserve the population package including candidate enumeration; source artifacts referenced not copied; design freeze not modified
Admit the population with STANDING_INHERITANCE = NONE and DESIGN_FREEZE_MODIFIED = FALSE
population_prerequisites: Enumerate all preserved source events reachable from main@56b4e064fa061417a82b7017f56d0dd98f225aa5 satisfying frozen ELG source-binding requirements
Record each candidate before evaluating Population 002 fit
Evaluate each candidate only against source-object identity, observable-manifestation distinctness, standing state, and source-binding completeness
Select the first qualifying combination under the predeclared ordering rule
Preserve qualifying but unselected candidates with ordering reason
Reject any selection influenced by a declared non-criterion
Create gallery entries that reference, not copy, source artifacts
Bind each entry's source coordinate to immutable commit hash, path, Git blob, and SHA-256 where available
Record boundary_made_observable with statement_origin and support_refs where applicable
Bind current_standing to standing_observed_at_commit, standing_source_path, and standing_source_identity
Do not promote standing for any referenced artifact
Preserve every non-claim declared in the design freeze and in this predeclaration
non_claims: CANDIDATE_ORDER = IMMUTABLE_SOURCE_COMMIT_ASCENDING THEN SOURCE_PATH_LEXICOGRAPHIC THEN MANIFESTATION_ID_LEXICOGRAPHIC
SAME_REPOSITORY + SAME_PREDECLARATION → SAME_CANDIDATE_DECOMPOSITION → SAME_BINDING_PER_CANDIDATE → SAME_ORDER → SAME_SELECTED_SET

predeclared_selection_rule.sequencing_claim: No event is selected or evaluated against the Population 002 selection procedure before this predeclaration is preserved
predeclared_selection_rule.note: Fork already knows its own history. The predeclaration freeze does not require or claim ignorance of preserved events. It requires that the selection procedure be frozen before any event is evaluated against it.

enumerated_surfaces.rule: each exterior return directory is a candidate source event; each distinct correction, finding, or observed manifestation within that return is a distinct candidate manifestation
each admission directory with a preserved object/event identifier is a candidate source event; each distinct preserved finding, discrepancy, or uncovered surface is a distinct candidate manifestation
each research object directory with preserved stage records is a candidate source event; each distinct preserved stage, attempt, or dimensional evaluation is a distinct candidate manifestation
each observation directory with a preserved event identifier is a candidate source event; each distinct preserved observation is a distinct candidate manifestation
each experiment directory with preserved run/procedural records is a candidate source event; each distinct run, attempt, or procedural record is a distinct candidate manifestation
NOT a candidate event surface; routing surfaces only

candidate_universe.constraint: A candidate exists iff the source event has an explicit preserved identifier AND the manifestation has a unique addressable preserved record within the canonical source artifact AND the frozen source-binding requirements are satisfied

canonical_source_binding_rule.rule: CANONICAL_SOURCE_BINDING = THE_IMMUTABLE_COMMIT + PATH + GIT_BLOB + SHA256 EXPLICITLY_DECLARED_BY_THE_PRESERVED_RECORD FOR_THAT_MANIFESTATION
canonical_source_binding_rule.note: If a preserved record declares multiple bindings without identifying one as primary, the candidate cannot be ordered until the source record is separately reconciled

manifestation_id_assignment_rule.rule: MANIFESTATION_ID = EXPLICIT_SOURCE_MANIFESTATION_ID WHERE_ONE_EXISTS; IF_NONE_EXISTS = ASSIGN ELG-CANDIDATE-MANIFESTATION-ID BY_FROZEN_DETERMINISTIC_RULE
manifestation_id_assignment_rule.source_local_record_offset_definition: ZERO_BASED_BYTE_OFFSET OF_FIRST_BYTE OF_THE_UNIQUE_ADDRESSABLE_MANIFESTATION_RECORD IN_CANONICAL_GIT_BLOB_BYTES, or the explicit finding/correction identifier declared by the source record if one exists; if neither is available, the candidate is an enumeration failure

byte_offset_precision.note: Measured against raw bytes of the canonical Git blob, not against any rendered, decoded, or display representation

candidate_universe.reproducibility_guarantee: SAME_REPOSITORY + SAME_PREDECLARATION → SAME_CANDIDATE_DECOMPOSITION → SAME_BINDING_PER_CANDIDATE → SAME_ORDER → SAME_SELECTED_SET

steps.action: Enumerate all source-event × observable-manifestation pairs in the candidate universe reachable from main@56b4e064fa061417a82b7017f56d0dd98f225aa5; record each with source-object identifier, manifestation identifier (explicit or generated), canonical source binding (commit + path + Git blob + SHA-256), and standing state
Record each candidate before evaluating Population 002 fit; candidate enumeration preserved as part of population package
Evaluate each candidate only against: source-object identity, observable-manifestation distinctness, standing state, source-binding completeness
Population 001 source event is enumerated for audit and is ineligible for Population 002 selection; if no qualifying set exists without it, there is no qualifying set
Select qualifying combination under byte-exact ordering rule and combination selection rule
Preserve qualifying but unselected candidates with ordering reason

population_001_reuse_edge.note: Population 001 source event is included in candidate enumeration for audit completeness. It is excluded from selection. No fallback to Population 001 reuse.

ordering_semantics.note: Eliminates ambiguity from case handling, locale, Unicode collation, normalization, decoded-character ordering, or display ordering; manifestation identifiers are encoded as UTF-8 and compared byte-by-byte in ascending order

combination_selection_rule.procedure: First, all qualifying event sets are identified. Among qualifying sets, the smallest cardinality set is preferred. If multiple qualifying sets share the smallest cardinality, the set whose sorted vector of candidate order indices is lexicographically earliest is selected.
combination_selection_rule.example: If candidates A,B,C,D are ordered as [1,2,3,4] and qualifying pairs exist at {A,C}=[1,3], {A,D}=[1,4], and {B,C}=[2,3], then {A,C}=[1,3] is selected because [1,3] is lexicographically earlier. No qualifying triple can outrank any qualifying pair.

example_boundary.note: Concrete examples of manifestation types are illustrative only and must not be treated as selection cues.
